To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the maximum margin criterion (MM) can be used to design effective feature extractors for dimensionality reduction, that the new feature extractor based on MM is stable and efficient, and that the nonlinear extension of the MM-based feature extractor is also effective.
we have established a new class of feature extractors that can be linear or nonlinear.

(1) the new linear and nonlinear feature extractors based maximum margin criterion are effective and efficient; (2) the new linear feature extractor does not suffer from small sample size problem; (3) the new feature extracters can be used for both feature extraction and classification.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new class of feature extractors, which are based on MMC.
the design of efficient and effective linear and nonlinear feature extractors.
the development of a novel class of efficient and robust feature extractors for pattern recognition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed feature extractors have the potential to be used as the standard feature extraction methods in many pattern recognition applications.
our proposed MMC-based feature extractors are very promising and have a lot of potential in real applications.
the new feature extraction techniques are superior to PCA, LDA and other existing feature extraction techniques.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MMC can be used as a unified criterion for feature extraction.
we have proposed a new class of feature extractors based maximum margin criterion (linear or nonlinear) and have shown their superiorities to the existing methods.
MMC can represent the class separability better, which is the most important criterion for feature extraction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
maximum margin criterion provides a very general principle for the design of feature extractors, and that the proposed MMC based methods are very promising for real-world applications.
the maximum margin criterion provides a powerful framework for designing new feature extractors.
maximum margin criterion is a useful principle for designing feature extractors.
